records.title: Introduction
headings: Message queues fur communication atween processes
records.text: We uise queuein theory in oor projects fur mony purposes: Hoo quick customer service answers Kanban plannin fur project management Message queues fur communication atween processes DevOps pipelines fur continuous deployment Hoo quick customer service answers Fur example, we want tae analyse hoo customers ask fur sales help an support help, an hoo quick we answer. Some relevant products are, fur example, Salesforce, LiveChat, Zendesk. Kanban plannin fur project management Fur example, we want tae track the lead times an progress times as an idea fur a new feature evolves fae design tae delivery. Some relevant products are, fur example, Asana, Jira, Microsoft Project. Message queues fur communication atween processes Fur example, we want tae maximise throughputs an minimise pressures as ae program sends requests tae anither program. Some relevant products are, fur example, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, ZeroMQ. DevOps pipelines fur continuous deployment Fur example, we want tae mak siccar that oor continuous integration server has the capacity tae test oor software an then deploy it. Some relevant products are, fur example, Jenkins, Bamboo, Azure DevOps.

records.title: Queue terms
records.text: Queue terms are a muckle topic. This section has some o oor common terms. Fur the examples, we will uise the idea o a customer waitin in line. Queue types an service types Queue types an service types describe hoo the queue chuises whit items tae process. First In First Out (FIFO): serve the customer that has been waitin the langest. Last In First Out (LIFO): serve the customer that has been waitin the shortest time. Priority: serve customers accordin tae their priority level; thir levels micht be based on status, urgency, payment, an sae on. Shortest Job First (SJF): serve the customer that needs the smawest amount o service. Longest Job First (LJF): serve the customer that needs the maist service. Shortest Remaining Processing Time (SRPT): like SJF, but a short job that has jist arrived can preempt a langer job that is awready in service. Round Robin: serve ilka customer fur a short time slice, then move on tae the next customer, an repeat. Time Sharing, aka Processor Sharing (PS): serve awbody at the same time; the service capacity is shared oot evenly amang awbody that is waitin. SJF an SRPT minimise the average wait, but they can starve lang jobs wi nae end, sae real systems aften add ageing or priority caps.

records.title: Notation o queue theory
headings: Throughput rates: total rate, success rate, failure rate, skip rate
Lead time, step time, wark time, wait time
records.text: Queue theory uises notation wi Greek letters. Oor teams uise some o the popular notation; we add some custom notation an aw that helps us wi software projects. Crosswalk fae oor notation tae the staundart textbook notation: Oors Staundart Meanin κ L average nummer o items in the system, waitin plus bein wrocht on λ λ arrival rate o items that enter the system μ μ service rate, aka capacity: hoo quick ae server warks while it is thrang ρ ρ utilisation: the fraction o time the servers are thrang, λ / (c μ) χ X throughput, aka departure rate: observed output, fur onie reason α nane success rate: observed output that turns oot richt β nane failure rate: observed output that turns oot wrang δ nane skip rate, aka dropoot rate: items that entered, then left wioot service ε nane error ratio β / (α + β) τ W average time in the system, aka lead time ω Wq average time waitin in the queue φ S average service time, aka wark time; μ = 1 / S θ nane step time atween completions; mean step time ≈ 1 / χ in steady state Please tak tent o symbol clashes when you read ither sources: σ uisually means staundart deviation, which is how we uise δ fur skip rate, an θ aften means the abandonment rate in Erlang-A call centre models, whauras we uise θ fur step time. Coont We coont items aften, an we uise this notation: κ (kappa): coont o items in the system, meanin items waitin plus items bein wrocht on Example: κ = 100 means there are 100 items in the system. κ > 100 means there are mair nor 100 items in the system. κ ≫ 100 means there are mony mair nor 100 items in the system. A coont sic as κ = 100 is a snapshot at ae moment. In Little's Law, κ means the lang-run average coont, which is the textbook L. The textbook symbol fur jist the items waitin in line is Lq. Arrival rate, service rate The maist important notation: λ (lambda): arrival rate. This meisures hoo quick new items are comin intae the queue. μ (mu): service rate, aka capacity. This meisures hoo quick ae server can haundle items while it is thrang. Examples o generalities fur traditional queues wi ae server: λ μ means the arrival rate is greater nor the service rate; the queue grows steadily, by aboot λ − μ items per time unit. The intuitive idea that "λ = μ keeps the queue the same size" is true anly when arrivals an service are perfectly regular, like a metronome. Real arrivals come in bursts, sae idle time lost in a lull can niver be gotten back, an the queue grows in the next burst. Please be awaur that some queuein theory practitioners uise "service rate" tae mean observed output raither nor capacity; see whit service rate means. Utilisation ratio, aka traffic intensity The maist important notation that sums up a queue: ρ (rho): utilisation ratio, meanin the fraction o time the servers are thrang = λ / μ fur ae server, or λ / (c μ) fur c servers Examples: ρ 1 means arrivals exceed capacity; the queue is gettin bigger. Throughput rates: total rate, success rate, failure rate, skip rate Throughput rates meisure observed output, meanin items that actually leave the queue. They come in fower braid categories: χ (chi): total rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time leave the queue fur onie reason: success, failure, skip, an sae on. α (alpha): success rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time period turn oot richt, fur example correct, complete, accepted. β (beta): failure rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time period turn oot wrang, fur example incorrect, incomplete, rejected. δ (delta): skip rate, aka dropoot rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time period enter the queue, then leave wioot bein served, fur example abandonments, reneges. Total rate = success rate + failure rate + skip rate: χ = α + β + δ (said: chi equals alpha plus beta plus delta) Ilka item coonted in χ entered the system, sae in steady state the total rate equals the arrival rate: χ ≈ λ. That is how throughput rates meisure output, no capacity. Whit service rate means Dependin on the context an the practitioner, the term "service rate" can mean either "total rate" or "success rate". This has historical ruits an can lead tae confusion an mistakes, maist o aw fur contexts an practitioners that uise queuein theory whaur there is a significant need tae track failures an skips. Theoretical View: The service rate is a pure meisure o speed (fur example, jobs per second), nae maitter whether the jobs are successes, failures, skips, an sae on. Processing View: The service rate includes whitever the queue spends time processin, meanin successes or failures, but disnae include skips. Technology View: In applied fields sic as software engineerin, the service rate meisures anly successes, whauras the error rate meisures failures, an the skip rate meisures dropoots. Sae we keep μ fur capacity, an we add observed output rates alangside it, raither nor replacin it: μ (mu): service rate, aka capacity. This meisures hoo quick ae server can haundle items while it is thrang. χ (chi): total rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time leave the queue fur onie reason: success, failure, skip, an sae on. α (alpha): success rate. This meisures hoo mony items per time period turn oot richt, fur example correct, complete, accepted. How no replace μ wi χ or α? In a stable queue, ilka item that enters leaves in the end, sae χ ≈ λ. Then λ / χ ≈ 1 whitever the load, which says naethin aboot hoo thrang the servers are. Utilisation needs capacity: ρ = λ / (c μ), which equals the fraction o time the servers are thrang. Skip rate Skip rate details: δ (delta): skip rate, aka dropoot rate. This meisures hoo mony items enter the queue, then leave wioot bein haundled. A skip is when an item enters the queue, then leaves wioot onie significant processin: Abandonin: when a customer jynes a queue, then leaves, fur onie reason. Renegin: when a customer that has awready waited decides tae leave because they hae wastit ower muckle time. Twa relatit behaviours are no skips: Balkin: when a customer decides no tae jyne the queue because the wait time threatens tae be ower lang. A balked item niver enters the system, sae it is ootwith the system boundary: it is no coonted in λ, χ, or δ. If balks maitter, sic as lost sales, then please coont them separately as turned-awa arrivals. Jockeyin: when a customer switches atween parallel queues, sic as checkoot lanes, tryin tae get a shorter wait. Error ratio The maist important notation that sums up a queue's success: ε (epsilon): error ratio = failure coont / (success coont + failure coont) = β / (α + β) Skips are left oot, because a skipped item wis niver serviced, sae it wis neither richt nor wrang. Please track skips separately wi δ. Examples: ε = 0 means nae errors. ε = 0.1 means 10% o services hae an error. ε = 1 means ilka service has an error. Lead time, step time, wark time, wait time We track fower times: τ (tau): lead time = fae the stert o the queue tae the end o the queue θ (theta): step time = fae ae finish tae the next finish; ae step time is ae gap, an the mean step time is the average gap φ (phi): wark time = time spent daein actual wark, aka processin time ω (omega): wait time = time spent no daein actual wark, aka pendin time Examples: τ = 5s means an item is added tae the queue, then serviced 5 seconds later. ω = 4s means an item waits in the queue fur 4 seconds, then wark sterts. φ = 1s means an item taks 1 second o wark, then is complete. θ = 1s means there is 1 second atween ae completion an the next completion. Relationships: τ = ω + φ: lead time is wait time plus wark time. In the examples, 5s = 4s + 1s. mean θ ≈ 1 / χ: in steady state, the mean step time is the inverse o the total rate. A single gap says little aboot the rate; the average o mony gaps says a lot. In the examples, if the mean step time is 1s, then χ ≈ 1 item per second. Staundart notation Staundart notation fur queuein theory describes a queue wi Kendall's notation, written as A/S/c/K/N/D: A: the arrival process, meanin the distribution o time atween arrivals. S: the service process, meanin the distribution o service times. c: the nummer o servers. K: the capacity, meanin the maximum nummer o items allowed in the system, waitin or bein served, afore new arrivals get turned awa. N: the population, meanin the nummer o potential customers. D: the discipline, meanin the queue type, sic as FIFO or LIFO. Common letters fur A an S: M: Markovian, aka memoryless, meanin exponential times, which arise fae Poisson arrivals. D: Deterministic, meanin constant times. G: General, meanin onie distribution. When the last three are left oot, the defaults are K = ∞, N = ∞, D = FIFO. Fur example, "M/M/1" means Poisson arrivals, exponential service times, ae server, unlimitit capacity, unlimitit population, an first in first oot. Staundart notation uises n an aw tae mean the nummer o items in the system.

records.title: Queue maths
records.text: The maths sections uise textbook symbols, sae that you can compare them wi ither sources: S is the average service time, which is oor φ, an μ = 1 / S is ae server's capacity. Please see the crosswalk in notation o queue theory. The utilisation curve The single maist important result in queuein theory: as utilisation gets near 100%, wait time grows wioot bound, an it grows quickest at the end. Fur an M/M/1 queue, whaur S is the average service time: Lead time τ = S / (1 − ρ) Wait time ω = S × ρ / (1 − ρ) Utilisation ρ Lead time τ Wait time ω 50% 2 × S 1 × S 70% 3.3 × S 2.3 × S 80% 5 × S 4 × S 90% 10 × S 9 × S 95% 20 × S 19 × S 99% 100 × S 99 × S Example: a code review taks 1 oor o wark. If reviewers are 80% thrang, a review taks aboot 5 oors fae request tae done. If reviewers are 95% thrang, it taks aboot 20 oors, even though the reviewers are anly 15 percentage points thranger. This is how "keep awbody 100% thrang" is a recipe fur lang lead times, an how the insichts ablow warn against plannin fur high utilisation. Kingman's formula Kingman's formula, aka the VUT equation, approximates wait time fur a single-server queue wi onie arrival an service distributions (G/G/1): ω ≈ (ρ / (1 − ρ)) × ((ca² + cs²) / 2) × S The three factors are: U: utilisation factor ρ / (1 − ρ), which is the utilisation curve abuin. V: variability factor (ca² + cs²) / 2, whaur ca is the coefficient o variation o time atween arrivals, an cs is the coefficient o variation o service times. The coefficient o variation is the staundart deviation dividit by the mean. T: time factor S, the average service time. Example: fur an M/M/1 queue, ca = cs = 1, sae V = 1, an the formula gies the same wait time as the utilisation curve. If you mak wark items mair uniform, sic as by splittin muckle tickets sae that cs draps fae 1 tae near 0, then V draps tae aboot 0.5, an the wait time is roughly halved at the same utilisation. Kingman's formula shaws the three levers fur reducin wait time: Reduce utilisation, sic as by addin capacity or limitin wark in progress. Reduce variability, sic as by smawer batches, mair uniform wark items, or smoother arrivals. Reduce service time, sic as by automation. Poolin an Erlang C Ae shared queue that feeds several servers is better nor separate queues that ilk feed ae server. This is how banks uise ae line that feeds mony tellers, an how a shared support queue beats a queue fur ilka agent. Example: twa servers ilk tak 1 oor per item, an items arrive at 1.6 items per oor in total, sae utilisation is 80%. Separate queues: ilka server is an M/M/1 queue wi 0.8 arrivals per oor, sae the lead time is 1 / (1 − 0.8) = 5 oors. Pooled queue: baith servers share an M/M/2 queue, sae the lead time is aboot 2.8 oors, which is aboot 44% less, wi the same fowk an the same wark. The Erlang C formula wirks oot the probability that an arrivin item maun wait in an M/M/c queue, wi offered load a = λ / μ an utilisation ρ = a / c: P(wait) = ((aᶜ / c!) / (1 − ρ)) / (Σₖ₌₀ᶜ⁻¹ (aᵏ / k!) + (aᶜ / c!) / (1 − ρ)) Wait time ω = P(wait) / (c μ − λ) Customer service teams uise Erlang C tae decide hoo mony agents tae staff tae meet a target, sic as "80% o calls answered within 20 seconds". Poolin has limits: it warks best when onie server can haundle onie item. If items need specialists, then a pooled queue micht need routin rules.

records.title: Trackin activities
records.text: Activity examples Suppose we hae somethin we want tae track, an we caw it somethin generic sic as "Activity", short fur "A". We can uise queuein notation efficiently tae describe the activity an hoo it moves through a queue. Examples: Aκ: Activity coont: hoo mony items are in the queue. Aλ: Activity arrival rate: hoo mony items are comin in per time unit. Aχ: Activity total rate: hoo mony items gang oot o the queue per time unit. Aα: Activity success rate: hoo mony items are richt per time unit. Aβ: Activity failure rate, aka error rate: hoo mony items are wrang per time unit. Aμ: Activity service rate, aka capacity: hoo mony items ae server can complete per time unit while thrang. Aδ: Activity skip rate, aka dropoot rate: hoo mony items are abandoned per time unit. Aρ: Activity utilisation ratio: the fraction o available time the servers are thrang, meanin thrang time ÷ available time, or λ / (c μ). Aε: Activity error ratio: hoo mony items are completit wi errors versus the total. Aτ: Activity lead time: hoo muckle time passes fae requested tae completit. Aω: Activity wait time: hoo muckle time passes fae requested tae stertit. Aφ: Activity wark time: hoo muckle time passes fae stertit tae completit. Aθ: Activity step time: hoo muckle time passes fae completit tae the next completit. Little's Law Little's law is a theorem by John Little that states: the lang-term average nummer L o customers in a stationary system is equal tae the lang-term average effective arrival rate λ multiplied by the average time W that a customer spends in the system. Example notation: L: lang-term average nummer o customers in the system. We prefer κ (kappa). λ: lang-term average effective arrival rate, meanin items that actually enter the system, sae excludin balks. W: lang-term average time an item is in the system. We prefer τ (tau). L = λ W is Little's law. We prefer κ = λ τ (kappa = lambda \ tau). Little's law is unco general: it hauds nae maitter the arrival distribution, the service distribution, the nummer o servers, or the queue type. Little's law assumptions: Aw meisurement units are consistent. The system is stable, meanin the average arrival rate equals the average departure rate ower the meisurement period, an the nummer o items is roughly the same at the stert an at the end. Items that leave early, sic as by renegin, are either coonted consistently in baith λ an τ, or left oot consistently fae baith. Example: a team has on average κ = 20 tickets in progress, an tickets arrive at λ = 4 per week; in steady state, the team finishes χ = 4 per week an aw. Sae the average ticket taks τ = κ / λ = 5 weeks. Tae cut lead time in hauf wioot warkin quicker, please cut wark in progress in hauf. Key performance indicators (KPIs) We track mony things aboot the activities in the queue, an we want tae sum up the results by chuisin a short leet o the maist relevant anes fur oor projects. We hae built mony projects, an we believe the maist valuable summary indicators are: Dτ = Delivery lead time. Product teams micht say "fae concept tae customer" or "fae idea tae implementation". Dα = Delivery success rate. DevOps teams micht say "deployment frequency" or "we ship X times a day". Dε = Delivery error ratio. Quality teams micht say "change fail rate" or "percentage o rollbacks". Rτ = Restore lead time. Site reliability engineers micht say "failed deployment recovery time" or "mean time to restore (MTTR)".

records.title: Service metrics
headings: Mean Time To Respond, Repair, Recover, Resolve
records.text: Uiseful terms: Service Level Indicator (SLI): is the metric (fur example, 99.9% uptime) Service Level Objective (SLO): the internal target fur that metric (fur example, aim fur 99.95% uptime) Service Level Agreement (SLA): the formal, contractual promise tae the customer (fur example, 99.9% uptime wi penalties if it is missed). Mean Time To Respond, Repair, Recover, Resolve MTTR stauns fur fower different meisurements: Metric Focus Meisures Stert Finish Mean Time To Respond First reaction Time tae acknowledge an stert action When the incident is detectit/reportit When the team sterts warkin on it Mean Time To Repair Technical fix Time tae fix the broken item When repair wark begins When the item is fixed Mean Time To Recover Service restoration Time tae restore full service When the incident/ootage sterts When the service is fully operational Mean Time To Resolve Complete resolution Total time fae detection tae closure When the incident is detectit When the incident is fully closed Key distinctions: Respond meisures team readiness an hoo weel alertin warks. A low response time means your monitorin an on-call processes are warkin weel, even if the actual fix taks langer. Repair is narrowly technical: hoo lang dis it tak tae actually fix the broken thing aince you are warkin on it? It excludes detection time, triage, an verification. Recover is aboot service availability fae the customer's point o view. The system micht be "repaired" but no yet "recovered" if you still need tae restore data, warm up caches, or verify functionality. Resolve is the maist comprehensive: it captures the hale incident lifecycle fae first detection through post-incident verification an closure. Example scenario: 2:00 AM — Ootage begins 2:05 AM — Alert fires, incident is detectit 2:15 AM — On-call acknowledges an sterts wark → Response time: 10 min (2:05 tae 2:15) 2:45 AM — Ruit cause identified, fix deployed → Repair time: 30 min (2:15 tae 2:45) 3:00 AM — Service verified warkin fur uisers → Recovery time: 60 min (2:00 tae 3:00) 3:30 AM — Incident ticket closed efter verification → Resolution time: 85 min (2:05 tae 3:30) Relatit metrics: MTBF (mean time before failure) MTTF (mean time to failure) MTTA (mean time to acknowledge) DORA metrics DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) metrics are industry-staundart key performance indicators (KPIs) specifically fur software engineerin DevOps teams. Please see dora.dev. DORA noo uises five metrics, in twa groups. Throughput metrics: Change Lead Time - Time tae implement, test, an deliver code fur a feature (meisured fae commit tae deployment in production). Please be specific aboot whit you mean by stert an finish. Fur example, some teams like tae meisure fae when a developer sterts wark on a ticket, tae when the developer pushes the wark tae a continuous integration process; this approach tends tae be mair effective fur meisurin personal productivity. Deployment Frequency - Nummer o deployments in a gien period o time. Please be specific aboot whit you mean by deployment an hoo you are trackin frequency. Fur example, some teams dae a deployment tae a fleet o production servers an track the full rollout, whauras ither teams dae a deployment tae a single user acceptance test (UAT) server an track when the project manager sends an email announcement tae the uisers askin them tae try testin. Failed Deployment Recovery Time - Time it taks tae recover fae a deployment that causes a failure in production. This wis formerly cawed Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) or Time to Restore Service. Please be specific aboot whit you mean by recovery. Fur example, some teams coont recovery as complete resolution, meanin the total time fae when an incident is detectit tae when an incident is fully closed; this approach is better describit as Mean Time To Resolve. Instability metrics: Change Failure Rate - Percentage o deployments that cause a failure in production an need immediate remediation, sic as a rollback or hotfix. Please be specific aboot whit you mean by failure. Fur example, some teams coont a failure an aw when they stert on a wark ticket then realise the wark ticket disnae hae eneuch information tae proceed, sae the team sends the wark ticket back tae the specification team. Deployment Rework Rate - Percentage o deployments that are unplanned, sic as tae fix a production incident. This is unplanned deployments dividit by total deployments. DORA added this metric in 2024. Earlier DORA reports discussed Reliability an aw as an operational performance metric: a braider, aften qualitative, assessment o service consistency, sic as availability, uptime, latency, accuracy, an service level objectives. Reliability helps shaw that high velocity disnae come at the expense o system capability.

records.title: Queue o queues
records.text: Queue theory is easy tae extend tae a queue o queues, sic as a heicher-level process that contains lower-level stages, or phases, or gates. Double Diamond queue o queues Fur example, consider the "Double Diamond" innovation process model, which specifies fower stages: Discover: Unnerstaund the issue raither nor jist assumin whit it is. Define: Wi insicht fae the discovery phase, define the challenge. Develop: Gie different answers tae the clearly defined problem. Deliver: Test different solutions at a smaw scale then improve them. Queue theory can model this as ae process queue that contains fower stage queues: The arrival rate o the process is the arrival rate o stage 1. The success rate o the process is the success rate o stage 4. The error coont o the process is the sum o the stages' error coonts. The skip coont o the process is the sum o the stages' skip coonts. The lead time o the process is the sum o the stages' lead times. The maximum throughput o the process is the throughput o the slawest stage, aka the bottleneck. Funnel queue o queues In oor practical wark, we aften uise the word "funnel" tae loosely describe a queue o queues that tends tae reduce the item coont at ilka stage: Hirin queue that uises an ootreach stage, interview stage, an offer stage. Fur this kind o queue, we aim tae maximise the stage 1 arrival rate, meanin increasin oor ootreach, sic as wi promotions. Purchasin queue that uises a customer search stage, shoppin cairt stage, an payment stage. Fur this kind o queue, we aim tae minimise the stage 2 skip rate, meanin reducin cairt abandonment, sic as wi reminders. Programmin queue that uises an integration stage, user acceptance stage, an production rollout stage. Fur this kind o queue, we aim tae minimise the error rate o the production rollout stage, sic as wi canary telemetry.

records.title: Insichts
records.text: Seiven insichts intae queuein theory, by Bob Wescott, author o "The Every Computer Performance Book" (please see Kottke's summary an aw): The slawer the service centre, the lower the maximum utilisation you should plan fur at peak load. It is gey hard tae uise the last 15% o onything. The closer you are tae the edge, the heicher the price fur bein wrang. Increases in response time are limitit by the nummer that can wait. Please mind this is an average, no a maximum. There is a human denial effect in multiple service centres. Please shaw smaw improvements in their best licht.
